## holt 0.4.0 — transactional recovery and bounded analysis

Install the signed, version-pinned GitHub release artifact:

```bash
npm install -g https://github.com/Raed2180416/holt/releases/download/v0.4.0/holt.tgz
```

The bare `holt` npm registry name is not an official distribution. Do not use
`npm install -g holt`, even if a package later appears there; use the exact GitHub release URL.

This release promotes the post-0.3.1 product and safety work through Holt's normal immutable tag
workflow. It is a product release, not evidence of customer adoption, a productivity rate,
universal host enforcement, or a commercial service.

### Integration operations are content-bound transactions

- Integration writes, removals, and receipt cleanup are conditional on the path identity and
  content observed at the start of the operation. A concurrent user or agent edit is preserved
  instead of overwritten or erased.
- The same initial receipt snapshot is carried across multi-worktree uninstall, closing the gap
  where a concurrent re-integration could otherwise be cleared by the final cleanup.
- Holt continues to alter only configuration entries it can identify as its own. Legal JSONC and
  unreadable or third-party configuration remain outside that ownership boundary.

### Analysis has a deterministic total work budget

- Glob analysis now charges bracket parsing and candidate traversal to one shared work budget.
  Large or adversarial candidate sets return a conservative result rather than consuming
  unbounded aggregate work.
- Content reads remain isolated from ambient Git filters and index flags. Platform aliases,
  sparse worktrees, ignored files, spaces, newlines, and Windows-native paths are retained in the
  evidence contract.

### Recovery and coordination remain explicitly separated

- Supported cleanup re-verifies candidates, moves only measured removable worktrees into locked
  local quarantine, and returns exact restore arguments; it does not physically delete their
  files or branches.
- Collision, duplicate, dependency, impact, order, and partition signals help coordinate parallel
  work but remain advisory. Exact content and recoverability evidence alone authorizes a
  destructive Holt action.
- Contract-tested host adapters are not described as live enforcement on every host. Arbitrary
  filesystem actions, unconfigured clients, and cloud agents remain outside Holt's authority.

### One release path and universal public-trust gates

- The alternate privileged fast-publish workflow has been removed. The protected stable-tag path
  owns quality, signing, installed-artifact verification, provenance, and immutable publication.
- Every pull request and main push emits a fail-closed required aggregate. Only an explicitly
  reviewed prose/site/legal surface can skip the heavyweight matrix; unknown paths run it.
- A universal trust lane checks installation copy, release bodies, security statements, website
  accessibility, and claim boundaries even when product code is unchanged.

### Verify this exact artifact

After downloading `holt.tgz` and the release assets:

```bash
gh release verify v0.4.0 --repo Raed2180416/holt
gh release verify-asset v0.4.0 holt.tgz --repo Raed2180416/holt
gh attestation verify holt.tgz --repo Raed2180416/holt
holt audit --require-signature
```

Each command verifies a different boundary. The detached manifest signature supports the offline
installed-tree audit; GitHub's immutable-release verification covers the release and asset; a
successful attestation query is the evidence for build provenance. Do not infer provenance if the
attestation query does not succeed.

For the full change ledger and remaining gaps, see the
[post-v0.3.1 55-commit audit](https://github.com/Raed2180416/holt/blob/v0.4.0/docs/research/2026-08-13-post-v0.3.1-55-commit-audit.md).
